claims.claim: Didymus the Blind was a Christian theologian who lived in Alexandria, Egypt, roughly between c. 313 and c. 398.
He was blind from early childhood, yet became a leading teacher of the Alexandrian catechetical school, a position appointed to him by Bishop Athanasius.
Didymus composed numerous volumes of biblical commentary, a major part of his scholarly output.
The papyrus codices containing Didymus’s works were discovered in 1941 by British engineers in a subterranean cavern at Tura, about ten miles outside Cairo.
After the Second Council of Constantinople (553) condemned Origen’s teachings, Didymus’s works fell into disrepute and were seldom copied, which explains why only fragmentary material survives today.
